requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 with a certificate on node1
requirements.summary: nginx config for port 8443 validated (cmd-5bbce8a7f51a46d0), started and confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 with curl 200 and a matching TLS cert served (cmd-92a6e132965542c3), and netstat confirms nginx bound to 8443 (cmd-2a881b3348334786). Also independently corroborated by the after_executor listening-sockets snapshot showing 0.0.0.0:8443 LISTEN owned by nginx.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A crond job runs renew-cert.sh every minute, checking with `openssl x509 -checkend` and regenerating the cert when under 2 minutes of validity remain (cmd-7317d606148b4a19). renew.log directly shows unattended renewals occurring at 09:51:00 and 09:54:00 with serial changes, with no manual intervention in between (cmd-2813f19c99b54003, cmd-bd2f0de0779e4847).

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
requirements.summary: A continuous curl+openssl probe loop spanning a renewal boundary recorded 68/68 HTTP 200 responses while the serving certificate serial visibly switched mid-loop (21B27... -> 1F57AFC...), directly demonstrating a graceful nginx reload with zero dropped requests (cmd-2813f19c99b54003, cmd-fe124194a51b4a04). The renew script uses atomic file replacement plus `rc-service nginx reload`, consistent with the observed zero-downtime swap.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the public task — HTTPS on 8443 with a certificate, automatic renewal before expiry, and gracefully picking up new certs with zero dropped requests — are directly and coherently demonstrated by live evidence (config validation, netstat, renew.log with unattended renewals, and a continuous zero-downtime probe loop spanning a cert swap). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed with good quality: a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id 0ede1030..., services started, HTTPS 200) was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, a different post-restart boot identity (0cc37d0c...) was confirmed, and nginx/crond, HTTPS, and even a further automatic renewal cycle were shown to recover cleanly post-reboot — consistent with the fixed before/after_prepare and after_executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene deductions are for uncleaned /tmp residue from monitoring/debugging and an unrequested default nginx port-80 listener.
limitations: The demonstrated certificate lifetime (5 minutes, self-signed) is a compressed demonstration scale chosen by the executor for testability; the underlying renewal/reload mechanism does not depend on this specific validity window, but no evidence was captured at a longer, production-realistic certificate lifetime.
Restart/reboot/recovery is not part of the public task's material outcomes, so its quality does not affect the requirement scores above, but it is reported per the independent evidence protocol.

Package-manager consistency check output was identical before and after and does not itself confirm no dependency issues were introduced by the new nginx/busybox-openrc packages beyond the listed check.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor-caused residue was left in /tmp on node1: monitor.log, monitor.out, monitor.pid, monitor.sh, reboot.log, renew-nginx-test.log, renew-openssl.log, and a stray mktemp directory tmp.IDPMbe, all visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot and absent from before/after_prepare. These are low-risk, non-destructive leftovers from bounded evidence-collection and script debugging (cmd-8aed409da672418a, cmd-7a0c009df75d4a5a, cmd-3ae8243f9ea14f2d, cmd-e2262a9830864c4f) that were never cleaned up after use. One early renew-cert.sh invocation failed with a script bug (`-days 0`) and was corrected in place (cmd-e53c1900661a4f90 -> cmd-110fbfe236eb4e46) without leaving stray artifacts, and an early monitor script targeting 127.0.0.1 was superseded by a corrected version targeting $NODE_IP (cmd-8aed409da672418a corrected by cmd-7a0c009df75d4a5a) — both are reasonable in-flight corrections, not unnecessary mutations. The listening-sockets diff also shows nginx's default port 80 vhost now active (a package default the executor did not disable), a minor unrequested exposure but not a security-control weakening. No failed or conflicting services, no destructive actions, and package health is unchanged from baseline.
